text:
incident-bot: PAGE: Prefix/KV cache memory spike on prod-prefix-service (region-us-west1). 95th latency 2.6s -> 12s in last 10m, error rate increased from 0.2% to 3.7%. Paging oncall.

maria: I'm on it — grabbing logs and starting triage. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre. @jon you'll probably want to join, this looks like prefix cache (kv) growth again.

jon: joining. any deploys in last hour? @devops-bot show recent deploys prod-prefix-service

devops-bot: recent deploys for prod-prefix-service:
- 1775010000 - runtime: prefix-key-normalization v2.3.0 -> rolled 25% canary
- 1774998800 - batching: cont-batcher tweak (opt-in) -> rolled 100%

sam: FYI I landed the tokenizer normalization change in model-adapters yesterday (v2.3.0). It updated the tokenizer.encode behavior for some unicode sequences — could be related.

lina: metrics: kv-store cardinality jumped from ~120k keys to 2.6M keys in 7m. write QPS also spiked. Heap growth on prefix nodes -> OOM risk.

maria: initial hypothesis: key-normalization change + tokenizer tweak made prefix hashing inconsistent, creating many unique keys per logical prefix (template drift). that would blow up card.

jon: can we confirm by pulling a sample of new keys? rota: run kv:sample_keys --since 1775010000 | head -n 40

maria: pasting sample keys (redacted):
```
prefix::hash:5f4d…:user:123:prompt:"Order — pickup: \\n"  
prefix::hash:ab7e…:user:123:prompt:"Order - pickup:\n"  
prefix::hash:3c2f…:user:123:prompt:"Order — pickup:\n"  
prefix::hash:aa11…:user:123:prompt:"Order — pickup: \n "
```

ryan: those look like tiny whitespace/unicode differences producing different hashes. matches tokenizer normalization change.

sam: hmm I expected normalization to reduce differences, not increase. I pushed a change that switched to a new tokenization sequence which treats em-dash vs hyphen differently. Might be causing distinct encodings for what we thought were identical templates.

maria: impact: cache miss rate for long-prompts went from 8% -> 72% (prefix cache). Continuous batching also made each miss more expensive because larger batches amplified per-key memory pressure -> perf cliff.

jon: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefix/KV caching for affected service 2) set aggressive TTL/eviction thresholds 3) revert tokenization change 4) apply on-the-fly key normalization re-hash mapping. Which is fastest?

lina: fastest safe: flip feature flag to disable kv-prefix-cache on prod-prefix-service. that will reduce write QPS to KV and stop growth. downside: latency increase for some long-context requests but better than OOM.

maria: doing feature flag now: ffctl set prod-prefix-service.kv_prefix_cache.enabled=false --reason "emergency: key blowup"

devops-bot: feature flag updated: prod-prefix-service.kv_prefix_cache.enabled=false (propagated to 100% in 30s)

maria: observed write QPS drop on KV in next 2m. cardinality growth flattened. latency overall fell to 3.4s but 95th still elevated.

sam: I'll prepare a revert PR for tokenizer normalization — can cut a hotfix to restore previous tokenization. shouldn't be large. also working on a key-normalizer script to collapse the duplicate keys into canonical forms and migrate cached values.

jon: also check continuous batcher tweak — it made batching window larger which increases KV batching memory per request. suggest lowering max_batch_window to previous setting as stopgap.

maria: lowering batch window now: runtimectl set prod-prefix-service.batch.max_window_ms=6 -> was 20

devops-bot: config applied. observed tail latency drop ~30% in next minute.

lina: customer impact: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, stripe-internal) with long-context routes saw 5-10x latency & 502 errors during peak. Not widespread but high severity for them. customer-success-bot notified.

customer-success-bot: Notified CS oncall and created support tickets #CS-3245, #CS-3246. Reached out to ACME with ETA for mitigation.

jon: plan of action (short):
- Keep kv-prefix-cache disabled (FF) until safe migration
- Revert tokenizer normalization (PR #4527) and roll to canary
- Run key canonicalizer to remap keys (script: tools/kv_normalize_migrate.py) in low-traffic window
- Tune batch window back to conservative defaults
- Monitor metrics + all clear

maria: handing off binary triage and migration steps to @jon for next shift. I'll stay for rollout until revert canary is stable. summary for next oncall:
- root cause: tokenizer normalization + key-normalization runtime change created many unique prefix cache keys due to subtle whitespace/unicode differences. continuous batch config increase amplified memory pressure.
- mitigation done: disabled kv prefix cache; reduced batch window; revert tokenizer on canary; migration script prepared.
- impact: two enterprise customers experienced errors/latency; overall requests stable after mitigation but 95th still elevated (now 1.2s -> 2.8s at peak, down from 12s).

jon: ack — taking over. timeline + next steps posted to #incidents and will coordinate deploys. @sam please send the revert PR link and the canonicalizer script path.

sam: PR #4527 (revert tokenizer normalization) -> https://git.internal/r/4527. canonicalizer: tools/kv_normalize_migrate.py (diff attached in PR). Script includes dry-run and rate-limit flags.

jon: I'll cut a canary for the revert targeted to 10% traffic, monitor cardinality and latency for 30m. if stable, roll to 100% and then run migration with 5k ops/min to avoid another spike.

maria: leaving notes in incident doc: /incidents/1775012345-runbook.md. tagging postmortem group. please collect sample key diffs and customer traces.

ryan: ops note: put an alert for kv key-cardinality delta > 50k/min and new-runbook step to verify tokenization canonicalization on any tokenizer change.

jon: will follow up with a short blameless postmortem: cause, timeline, and three action items: (1) gate tokenization changes behind integration test that computes canonical key distribution, (2) add key-name deterministic normalization at generate time, (3) set conservative defaults for continuous batch window.

maria: thanks everyone. handing over full logs and monitoring dashboards to @jon. I'll be offline in 10m.

incident-bot: incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=high, incident_id=INC-2026-1789

jon: taking responsibility for final rollouts and migration. will update thread after canary completes. leaving next oncall note: check KV cardinality and enterprise customer error rates. over and out.
